answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks via mandatory original submissions scored by peer juries on a public ledger. To earn, each identity must produce novel text explaining mechanisms, incorporating markers such as yarrow, jetty, and garden. An attacker creating fakes faces repeated generation costs for unique content that must survive jury grading; failed or duplicated efforts yield zero coins while consuming inference compute, rendering large-scale identity farming economically unviable as the network detects and rejects non-original work.
